TOMISLAV MESARIĆ
Butcher | Meat Counter Assistant

CONTACT
Email: [EMAIL]
Phone: [PHONE]
Location: [CITY]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Butcher-trained meat counter professional with four years of customer service experience and practical skills in meat preparation, sausage making, stock rotation and daily hygiene routines. Experienced in preparing whole lambs and suckling pigs for events, weighing and pricing customer orders, and maintaining cold-room stock using FIFO. Basic HACCP knowledge.

KEY SKILLS
• Meat preparation and butchery
• Meat counter customer service
• Weighing and pricing orders; till operation
• Fresh sausage production and recipe development
• FIFO stock rotation and cold-room routines
• Basic HACCP knowledge and hygiene checks
• Cleaning slicers, mincers and counter areas
• Hand pallet jack use
• English for customer service

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Butcher / Meat Counter Work | Mesnica Kod Ante | 2020–Present
• Prepare fresh sausages, producing approximately 40 kg per week during the busy season.
• Developed the shop’s lamb merguez recipe and adjusted the ćevapi mix to 70% beef and 30% lamb following customer feedback.
• The shop’s ćevapi won second place at the Zagreb County craft meat fair in 2023.
• Prepare whole lambs and suckling pigs for spit-roasting events, including ordering, butchering, seasoning and morning delivery.
• Completed orders for three weddings and approximately ten family parties annually from 2022 to 2025; the largest was four lambs and two pigs for a 180-guest wedding in Samobor in 2024.
• Ran a six-week dry-ageing trial on beef ribs at 21 and 28 days, recording weight loss and temperature. The shop now sells dry-aged rib by pre-order, approximately 15 kg per month.
• Rotate cold-room stock each morning, placing older stock at the front.

Meat Counter Service | Dolac Market Hall | Four years
• Serve customers at a meat stall; weigh and price orders and operate the till.
• Clean slicers and the mincer at the end of each day.
• Wrote a one-page closing and cleaning checklist for the slicer, mincer, counter and floor drain following a hygiene inspection remark in 2017. The checklist remains in use at the stall.

EDUCATION & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Butcher Training | Food Trades School | Completed 2015
Preparing for the Master Butcher Examination (majstorski ispit), Chamber of Trades | Planned spring 2027; not yet passed

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
HACCP: Basic knowledge
Equipment: Hand pallet jack experience; no forklift licence

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, focused CV with a clear target title, relevant professional summary, standard section headings, and quantified evidence. The experience is particularly persuasive: sausage production volume, recipe development, an award result, event orders, dry-ageing results, and the cleaning checklist demonstrate practical skill, initiative, and reliability. The document is professional and easy to scan. Minor limitations are that some duties relevant to the advertised supermarket environment—such as portioning, packaging, temperature recording, and customer advice on cuts or preparation—are not stated as explicitly as they could be. The planned Master Butcher Examination is correctly described as not yet passed, which avoids overstating the qualification.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses simple headings, conventional bullet points, standard date ranges, and relevant keywords including butcher, meat counter, customer service, FIFO, HACCP, sausage production, weighing, pricing, till operation, and stock rotation. Its likely AI/ATS screening probability is high for the stated must-have requirements. To improve matching further, use the job ad's exact operational terms where supported, especially "cut," "portion," "package," "temperature checks," and "hygiene checks." The current company-and-role formatting is understandable, but separate employer, job title, and dates more clearly to improve parsing consistency.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV shows a very strong match for the two must-have requirements: completed butcher training and substantially more than two years of meat-counter experience, plus HACCP knowledge. It also aligns well with FreshCart's emphasis on knowledgeable customer service, FIFO rotation, hygiene, product knowledge, reliability, and pride in good work. The candidate's experience with whole lambs and suckling pigs, fresh sausage production, customer feedback, and dry-ageing adds valuable product knowledge. Gaps in the candidate's material include no forklift licence, no supermarket experience, no experience with tray sealers or self-service labelling scales, and only basic HACCP knowledge rather than advanced HACCP training. The CV should not imply those capabilities. The document also does not explicitly demonstrate advising customers on cuts and preparation or maintaining a 95% peak-time shelf/counter stock level, although those are not established in the candidate's source material.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS AND ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, change "practical skills in meat preparation, sausage making, stock rotation and daily hygiene routines" to "practical skills in cutting and preparing meat, fresh sausage production, FIFO stock rotation and daily cleaning routines." Use "cutting" only in the context of the documented butchery work, and retain "cleaning" because it is directly supported by the source information.
2. In the Key Skills section, change "Cleaning slicers, mincers and counter areas" to "Cleaning and maintaining slicers, mincers and meat-counter areas" to use the job-relevant term "meat counter" while remaining truthful.
3. In the Mesnica Kod Ante experience section, revise the dry-ageing bullet to read: "Ran a six-week dry-ageing trial on beef ribs at 21 and 28 days, recording temperature readings and weight loss; the shop now sells approximately 15 kg of dry-aged rib per month by pre-order." This makes the documented temperature-recording experience easier for ATS screening to identify.
4. In the Dolac Market Hall experience section, add a truthful packaging-related bullet based on the candidate's notes: "Wrap customer meat orders in paper after weighing and pricing." Do not describe this as tray sealing, self-service packaging, or labelling-scale experience, because those capabilities are not in the candidate's background.
5. In the Education & Professional Development section, retain the wording "Planned spring 2027; not yet passed" after the Master Butcher Examination. Do not shorten this to "Master Butcher" or present it as a completed qualification.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "hygiene checks"

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, relevant CV with clear sections, credible responsibility statements, and unusually useful quantified evidence: approximately 40 kg of sausage per week, three weddings and about ten family events annually, a 180-guest wedding, a 15 kg monthly dry-aged product, and a second-place competition result. The summary and skills section quickly establish butcher training, counter service, FIFO, cleaning, and HACCP knowledge. The main content issue is an unclear employment timeline: Mesnica Kod Ante is listed as 2020–Present, while Dolac Market Hall is described only as “Four years,” although the candidate’s original material says he currently works at the Dolac stall. The CV should make the relationship and dates of these roles unambiguous. The planned Master Butcher Examination is accurately labelled as not yet passed, which is professionally responsible.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly overall: it uses standard headings, simple bullet points, searchable terms such as “butcher,” “meat counter,” “HACCP,” “FIFO,” “fresh sausage,” “weighing,” “pricing,” “till,” and “cold-room,” and avoids tables, graphics, columns, and complex formatting. Its likely ATS/AI screening probability is high for the stated must-have requirements because completed butcher training, more than two years of meat-counter experience, and HACCP knowledge are explicit. ATS alignment could be slightly improved by using the job’s exact phrase “cut, portion and package fresh meat” only where truthful and supported; the current CV demonstrates cutting/preparation and paper wrapping, but does not support self-service tray sealing or supermarket labelling. The unexplained “Four years” date entry may reduce chronology parsing and should be clarified.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV shows both mandatory requirements: completed butcher training and HACCP knowledge. It also aligns well with the role’s core work through meat preparation, customer orders, weighing and pricing, till operation, FIFO stock rotation, cold-room routines, cleaning, sausage production, and event preparation. The candidate’s product knowledge and customer-facing experience support FreshCart’s emphasis on knowledgeable, friendly counter service, reliability, hygiene, and pride in good work. The forklift licence is a gap, not a document defect: the candidate has hand pallet jack experience but explicitly has no forklift licence. The candidate’s notes also show no supermarket experience and no experience with tray sealers or self-service labelling scales. The CV does not claim these unsupported skills, which is correct. Formal temperature and hygiene check recording is not clearly demonstrated; the dry-ageing temperature records are relevant but are not the same as routine HACCP checks, so this should not be presented as equivalent.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Experience section under “Meat Counter Service | Dolac Market Hall,” replace the standalone date label “Four years” with a clearer, truthful date/status description based on the candidate’s actual employment history. If the Dolac work overlapped with Mesnica Kod Ante, state that accurately, for example: “Four years; concurrent meat-counter service work” only if that is factually correct. The goal is to explain how this role relates to the separate 2020–Present Mesnica role without inventing dates or employment status.
2. In Additional Information, consider deleting “no forklift licence” while retaining “Hand pallet jack experience.” The job lists a forklift licence only as a plus, and foregrounding a non-required absence uses valuable CV space; do not imply forklift operation or certification.
3. In the Professional Summary, consider changing “practical skills in cutting and preparing meat” to “practical skills in cutting, preparing and packaging customer meat orders” only if the candidate’s paper-wrapping work is intended to be represented as packaging. Do not add tray sealing, self-service labelling, routine HACCP temperature checks, or supermarket experience because those are not supported by the original candidate information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, focused CV with a clear target title, relevant summary, useful quantified achievements, and good evidence of butchery, sausage production, customer service, FIFO stock rotation, hygiene routines, and event preparation. The project-style achievements make the experience more credible and memorable. The main content concern is employment chronology: the CV presents Mesnica Kod Ante as the current employer while the original candidate information says the candidate currently works at the Dolac meat stall. The Dolac entry also gives only “Four years” rather than dates. This should be resolved for complete credibility. The CV also lacks contact details, which reduces practical usability for an application.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly overall: it uses standard section headings, simple bullet points, searchable job terminology, and no problematic tables, graphics, columns, or icons. Strong matching keywords include “butcher,” “meat counter,” “meat preparation,” “fresh sausage production,” “FIFO,” “HACCP,” “weighing,” “pricing,” “till,” and “cold-room stock.” AI screening probability is high because the role fit is immediately clear and supported by concrete evidence. critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV clearly meets both must-have requirements: completed butcher training and more than two years of meat-counter experience, plus basic HACCP knowledge. It aligns especially well with FreshCart’s needs for fresh meat preparation, customer-facing counter service, weighing and pricing, FIFO rotation, hygiene, cold-room routines, and product knowledge. The recipe development, customer-feedback adjustment, dry-ageing trial, and event orders demonstrate care and pride in the product. Forklift licensing is a genuine gap, but it is correctly disclosed and is only a nice-to-have. The candidate’s material also shows no supermarket experience and no experience with tray sealers or self-service labelling scales; these are role-related limitations rather than defects in the CV and should not be misrepresented. The CV does show transferable paper-wrapping, weighing, pricing, cleaning, stock, and temperature-recording experience.

Use the accurate dates and clarify whether these were separate, concurrent, or sequential roles. Do not leave “Present” in both places unless that is factually correct.

2. In the header, add the candidate’s accurate phone number and professional email address if available. Do not invent contact details. This is important for recruiter usability and application completeness.

MINOR:
3. In the Dolac Market Hall experience section, replace the vague date label “Four years” with the verified employment date range. This will improve ATS parsing and remove ambiguity.

4. In the Professional Summary or relevant experience bullet, change the wording to include supported job-ad terminology without overstating experience. For example, revise “practical experience in meat preparation” to “practical experience cutting and preparing fresh meat, weighing and packaging customer orders, and serving a meat counter.” Keep “packaging” limited to the supported paper-wrapping experience; do not claim tray-sealer or self-service-pack experience.
